text: It also goes without saying that the early years of a child are a critical period.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Tapping into their growth potential through early intervention ensures greater independence in their later years.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Children with disabilities, like all Singaporean sons and daughters, have the same access to the Child Development Account (CDA).

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: They could use the funds in the CDA to pay for childcare centres, kindergartens or even assistive technology like hearing aids.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: While it is heartening to see an inclusive range of services that caters to most needs, assistive technology can become very expensive very quickly.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Here I pause to ask if MSF can consider more financial support through the First Step Grant or boosting co-matching of the savings of such parents.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: By enhancing support, we not only ease their financial burden, but also send a strong message to these parents that the Government stands with them, recognises their added challenges and is committed to ensuring that all children have an equal start to life.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Today, there are many support schemes available for persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: We live in a blessed age and we can be thankful for much.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Among these schemes, some use a means-testing approach.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: This is a good thing – it is sensible to allocate more to those in greater need.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: While those in extreme circumstances surely benefit, I worry if these schemes place the same support out of reach for many other Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: The ATF has the potential to greatly aid persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: When used in early intervention, assistive technology offers immense benefits to children with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: For instance, a quality pair of hearing aids can cost thousands of dollars to purchase.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: And then there are also regular maintenance costs to account for.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: They provide enhanced sound quality, crucial for early language development and social communication.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: To be eligible, per capita household gross monthly income must strictly fall below S$2,000.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, there is the Enabling Transport Subsidy (ETS), which subsidises dedicated transport fees.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Among others, children with disabilities attending early intervention programmes can benefit.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Again, the reach of the ETS is limited.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: For Singaporeans to access the subsidy, per capita household gross monthly income must be no more than S$2,800.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: This means a typical household with substantial assistive technology and transport expenses would not be supported by these schemes.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: These families, often with one full-time caregiver, need and deserve help, too.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: To address this, could we consider revising the income threshold of such schemes to align with median per capita household income?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Or, perhaps, look beyond household income as the basic qualifying criteria.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: This further calibrates our approach, ensuring that our well-intentioned policies truly serve those in need.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: To share my own personal experience, I was born with Osteogenesis Imperfecta.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: During the most challenging period of my childhood, I could sustain up to six fractures a year.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I was confined at home, often in a cast, when my friends were out there playing in the sun.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Needless to say, frequent hospital trips, treatment and surgeries also meant that medical costs were high.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Raising children is already a monumental task for most young parents.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Caring for children with disabilities adds to the cognitive load.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, my parents were unwavering in their care.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: They are the reason why I have become who I am today.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Up until junior college, my father drove me religiously to school and back.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: My mother made the swift decision to become a full-time caregiver shortly after I was born.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: During primary school, she accompanied me daily, buying food for me during recess and helping for toilet breaks.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: She even tried to find ways to enrich my learning, bringing me to art and piano classes, long before it was obvious I had zero artistic talent.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Not all parents have the same ability or resource to do what mine did for me.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: For struggling parents, finding opportunities to enrich their children's lives can be overwhelming.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Some just need a bit more help, some encouragement and support.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: We need to encourage all parents to look at their child as beacons of potential, despite disability.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Learned helplessness must be unlearnt right from the beginning.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Children with disabilities can grow up to become world-class musicians, neuroscientists or elite athletes.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: We have living examples right here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Clearly, disability alone does not prevent one from success.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In July 2021, the PAP Women’s Wing and Young PAP jointly presented a paper on women’s development.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Titled "Take Action for Women in Singapore", it was drafted based on our engagements with over 1,500 people comprising different age groups and backgrounds who were surveyed on issues faced by women in schools, workplaces and home.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One recommendation which I resonate with – and more particularly so currently as an expectant working mother in my third trimester – and of which I have been advocating for during the White Paper debate on Singapore Women’s Development in April last year, is to further encourage equal sharing of childcare responsibilities amongst mothers and fathers – something that we have aimed to achieve since as early as 1961 when the Women’s Charter was first enacted.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Section 46 of the Act specifically sets out that "upon the solemnisation of marriage, the husband and the wife shall mutually bound to cooperate with each other… in caring and providing for the children" and "the husband and wife shall have equal rights in the running of the matrimonial household."  Increasingly so, fathers are playing a more active and significant role in caring for their children, from bringing their kids for medical appointments to walking them to and back from school.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My Woodgrove residents have often shared with me that the role a father plays has been expanding and this is keenly felt within each family.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many more fathers have also been seen doing so, signifying a change in public attitude towards the sharing of parental responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Notwithstanding, the rebalancing exercise sought to be undertaken by this Bill should also be accompanied by a re-examination of the support given by the state in order to ensure that it remains fair to our children, mothers, fathers and, not to forget, the employers.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I, therefore, applaud the additional enhancements which will be introduced through this amendment Bill, such as the increment of Government-paid paternity leave and other benefits.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Nevertheless, I wish to take this opportunity to seek several clarifications and make several suggestions.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This was one of the recommendations set out in our Women’s Development recommendation paper.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Currently, a working mother can share up to four weeks of her 16-week maternity leave with her husband.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In relation to this, I would further urge the Government to consider providing full flexibility to all couples to decide how they wish to share their maternity and paternity leave between themselves.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Through my many interactions with the young parents that I have met in Woodgrove during our Embracing Parenthood-themed community engagements as well as during my house visits, I have realised that there is no-one-size-fits-all solution for parental leave arrangements.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Every family has its own unique set of circumstances and preferences.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Some mummies may prefer to have their husband to play a more supportive and active role after childbirth as they look forward to resuming work sooner, while others would much prefer their maternity leave to be extended further so that they can fully concentrate on their new-found state of motherhood, nursing their children and being present for significant milestones before returning to work.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My second point pertains to clarifications on the period of a female employee commencing her Government-paid maternity leave.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, we have seen cases where expectant mothers have had to be warded for more than 28 days from their estimated or actual delivery date or were intermittently required to go on medical leave for treatment even before their child was delivered due to pregnancy complications.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In such situations, the working mothers had to rely on their own paid or unpaid medical leave as they were still considered ineligible for Government-paid maternity leave.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For example, instead of a continuous period of no earlier than 28 days from the date of confinement, could expectant mothers be given the aggregate 28 days of Government-paid maternity leave that may be consumed in their final trimester?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Or while all medical appointments are important and necessary, there are some which are straightforward and which will not take the full working day.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For situations, such as this, could the Bill perhaps provide for the flexibility of the "time-off" and/or half-day consumption of such leave days?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: When I attended Woodgrove’s Bonding with your Child Day just yesterday alongside 80 of our Woodgrove residents with young children at an indoor activity playground theme park, I took the opportunity to gather more feedback about the challenges faced by our young parents.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For example, monies in their child’s CDA can be utilised to pay for preschool fees, but not the optional extracurricular activities organised by the preschools.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Fourth point is in relation to the introduction of family care leave.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These issues would, of course, vary from household to household, for example, managing the effects of post-partum depression for mummies; accompanying toddlers for speech therapy sessions; or attending to the medical needs of ageing parents or relatives and so on.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The fifth point and my final clarification pertains to employers’ buy-in.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While we strive to achieve conditions that will better support Singaporeans to embrace families, I am also mindful that we must take care to ensure that employers’ interests are not forsaken as this will ultimately affect the livelihood of the employees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Societal norms, work and family structures are evolving.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Families are faced with competing caregiving responsibilities for their young and old.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Fathers want to actively participate in their child’s upbringing, and both fathers and mothers want to share the duty of caring for their elderly parents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: These amendments can help families to better cope with their caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Fathers will have the support and encouragement to be more engaged and present in the precious moments of their children's lives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It will also indirectly help to provide support to their wives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I will also be highlighting the importance of workplace support in line with the proposed enhancements.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The enhancement is a clear signal of the Government's steadfast commitment to supporting fathers in their pursuit of shared parental responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: These enhancements will benefit both employed and self-employed fathers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This transition period is critical for employers to adapt their work and operational systems to the new normal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Some companies have taken the lead, such as H&M and Electrolux, which are amongst some of our nation’s employers who have taken an early start in providing paid paternity leave of four weeks since 2022.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Standard Chartered Bank has taken a giant leap by offering 20 weeks of paid paternity leave.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is commendable, but at the same time, I recognise that not all companies can do likewise and will need time to adapt.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But clearly, companies see this as an important HR policy and have taken the lead to do so.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Would the Ministry consider also setting a clear timeline on when the enhanced GPPL benefit will be made mandatory?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Such a clear signpost would give both clarity and impetus to companies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In legislating these enhancements, we must also recognise the importance of supportive workplaces and awareness regarding the enhanced GPPL.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Many fathers would be assured if their management comes out strongly to support them in taking leave to care for their newborn.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Ensuring that eligible fathers are well-informed of the benefits will enable them to make full use of their GPPLs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Ministry broaden its work with the trade associations and chambers, and the Labour Movement to spread such support and awareness?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This becomes even more critical for self-employed fathers, such as freelancers and gig workers, who may not have the same level of workplace support and awareness of such schemes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Next, a requirement for self-employed fathers to be eligible for GPPL is that they must be engaged in a particular trade, business, profession or vocation for a continuous period of at least three months before the child’s date of birth.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This effectively means that the self-employed father would have to be working continuously until the date of the child’s delivery.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: There would be instances where the self-employed father would need to support his wife in the pre-delivery phase.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I hope that we can provide flexibility in meeting the continuous three months criteria.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It would help our self-employed fathers to cope with their responsibilities better.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Enhancing the UICL by six days per parent per year for children under two is important.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Parents would know that young children under two require frequent visits to the doctor.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: There would be routine checks and the unavoidable catching of viruses and bugs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The UICL will indeed go some way in helping parents attend to the needs of their children while being employed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: To enhance the usefulness of the UICL, we should enhance the flexibility of its usage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Rather than mandating that employees take the entire entitlement of the proposed 12 days in a single year, it would be beneficial to allow parents to use it flexibly during the child's first two years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Moreover, could the Ministry consider a measured increase in the number of UICL days based on the number of children?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Families with multiple young children may have different caregiving needs, and tailoring their allowances accordingly would be a good step forward.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Furthermore, we must also address the concerns of parents facing financial constraints, as the UICL is currently unpaid.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We must ensure that the intended benefits of UICL are accessible to families across the socio-economic spectrum, including low-income workers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It might be difficult for low-income workers to use the UICL.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Perhaps we could consider offering a partial subsidy or support for lower-wage workers in taking the UICL.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This would alleviate financial burdens and make it more feasible for them to utilise this support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: One of the commonly cited reasons was the lack of workplace support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Promoting such a workplace culture can start small, beginning with raising awareness among employees about the availability and importance of paternity leave.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The longer-term goal would really be to dispel stigmas associated with men taking time off for family responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Offering flexible work arrangements, such as remote work options or adjusted schedules, can further facilitate fathers' involvement in childcare without compromising their professional commitments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Additionally, companies can provide resources, like parenting workshops or support groups, to help fathers navigate their roles and responsibilities more effectively.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We can also similarly develop such programmes for fathers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Such initiatives exemplify the corporate world's potential to contribute to the well-being of families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Employers should look into implementing such programmes for both mothers and fathers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Where required, the union, the Labour Movement, stands ever ready to help our SMEs with developing such policies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: However, there are also families facing pressures with having to care for both the young and elderly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The families that we are supporting today to raise their young children would also need support to care for their parents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The instances when they have to bring their elderly parents to the doctor are comparable to that for their young children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We must not forget that our workers who are single would also face caregiving responsibilities for their elderly parents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: They signify a progressive stride towards recognising and facilitating fathers' active involvement in their children's lives.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is now my pleasure to call on Ms Usha Chandradas for her maiden speech.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: But I have some comments to make that I hope the Government will take into consideration.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: It aims to reset traditional perceptions that child rearing should be the sole responsibility of mothers.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: In some ways, these legislative changes are in step with what is already happening in multinational enterprises, in recognition of how the world is changing.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, Minister of State Sun Xueling mentioned the example of Telstra as a business that has already started to adopt expansive family friendly policies.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Standard Chartered Bank is another example that I would like to cite.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Employees at Standard Chartered Bank will now get a minimum of 20 weeks of paid parental leave "irrespective of gender", or how a child comes to permanently join an employee’s family.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: HSBC also recently announced extended paternity and maternity leave for its employees.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: While the present legislative amendments that we are addressing today, do not go as far as what these private institutions have done, they signal to me the Government’s broad commitment towards adapting and making changes where necessary, when traditionally-held societal norms start to change.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Whether it is a question of perhaps, eventually equalising maternity and paternity leave entitlements, or perhaps giving recognition to the needs of different kinds of family units, it is my hope that the Government continues to keep pace with the times and that it will display the same fortitude in future policy reform that it has demonstrated today with these proposed amendments.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: With the present expansion of paternity leave, it is also important to bear in mind that pressing family needs may well go beyond the care of children and newborns.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: We are very concerned in Singapore about our falling fertility rates, but let us also not forget that we have a rapidly ageing population.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: By 2030, almost one in four Singaporeans will be over the age of 65.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: While there is much discourse about empowering our elders to continue learning, working and remaining productive for as long as possible, it remains critical that we acknowledge and find solutions towards supporting those who are no longer able to work.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Frail elders are more likely to suffer from chronic health issues and are thus more likely to require full-time caregiving.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: As our population ages, more seniors will need care and there will accordingly be more caregivers who will need support.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: While we enhance leave entitlements for the care of newborns, better support for caregivers of the elderly remains just as important an area for policy-makers to look into.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: While flexible working arrangements go some way towards alleviating caregiver stress, they also fundamentally assume that eldercare duties are not serious or taxing enough to require dedicated days off from work.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Flexible work arrangements also do not necessarily assist self-employed persons.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Certain communities, for example, the arts community, have large percentages of its members in self-employed roles.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: In the arts, according to the latest Singapore Arts Plan, at least one-third of the workforce operates on a self-employed basis.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Feelings like these, if left to simmer and brew, will only result in greater workplace tension and resentment, and these may well reverse any positive steps taken towards the ending of maternity discrimination.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: The changes proposed today are very welcome ones towards "ungendering" workplaces.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: These changes will render much-needed support to workers, in recognition of the many challenges of family life.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: It is my fervent hope the Government continues this push towards inclusiveness and the caregiving needs of our country as a whole and as societal norms continue to grow and evolve over time.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Back in the day, when families were larger and when extended families lived together, there were economies of scale in households to take care of the young, almost by the batch.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Close neighbourly relationships also meant that there was usually a set group of women in the neighbourhood who would help with babysitting.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Labour Movement appreciates that the Ministry has listened to our workers' feedback and has considered our calls for more caregiving leave.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The amendments to this Bill is a great start to supporting Singaporean families by providing them with additional resources to alleviate their financial and time pressures and indeed, it makes allowances for fathers to be more present during the early development of their child.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, two practicalities need to be taken into consideration in the roll-out of such leave support: (a) the workplace cultural norms which need to be developed to catch up with legislative calls for more parental leave; and (b) the long-term sustainability of continually increasing paid and unpaid parental leave for workers as well as businesses.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Let us talk about the current state of workplace norms.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The reality is that for many workers, when it comes to taking time-off from work, it is sometimes a sticky conversation.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Workplace policies to create allowances for working parents do not necessarily translate to these allowances being realised.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In an ideal world, the process goes like this.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: A working parent is faced with a home emergency.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They approach their employer with a leave request which is readily approved and the working parent goes on leave to resolve the situation.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many face the dilemma of how taking more time away from work may negatively impact the impression their bosses and colleagues have of them.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They may worry about their career progressions at work, or even finding alternative employment if they find themselves victims of discrimination.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: If you think about it, how many times has the "office" congratulated a "co-worker" on the birth of their child, while also in the same breath, complained of how much more "productive" they need to be as they cover their colleagues' work while they are away on leave.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Of course, the unions have our workers' back should they be faced with unfair treatment, but many working parents seek for favourable work relationships, choosing not to rock the boat and thus not fully utilising their full entitlement.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Providing more paid leave for working parents and caregivers to tend to their families is welcomed, but we need our work cultures and work arrangements to catch up with legislative moves.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While we empathise with new parents who feel the sheer physical exhaustion, especially sleep deprivation, that comes with taking care of a newborn infant, let us also not forget the many other types of familial duties – parents with older kids who need help in school, or in navigating the sensitive period that is adolescence; parents who are raising children with special needs; and sandwiched working parents who are also caregivers to elderly parents or relatives.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: These are the everyday caregiving burdens that many households in Singapore face today – the challenge of juggling of work and family.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: All of these efforts require more than just a few weeks of time away from work.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is an intense balancing act, constantly juggling between responsibilities at home and commitments at work.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is a lifelong balancing act that perhaps, calling for leave, is just a start.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is therefore timely that we begin to explore more sustainable options for work-life harmony to complement the increasing number of days of leave.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Labour Movement has been advocating for flexible work arrangements (FWAs) for decades, and we continue to believe that FWAs is the catalyst for changing workplace norms when it comes to work-life harmony and it is the long-term solution to keeping our working parents in the workplace.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: During the pandemic, FWAs were implemented as the defacto way to work and companies scrambled to find ways to implement FWAs with existing technologies and resources.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In the post-pandemic modern workplace, companies have started conversations with their workers on implementing enforceable, practical policies around providing FWAs as a long-term solution.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: FWAs are not only about working from home but FWAs can mean flexi-time, flexi-place and even flexi-load.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: FWAs are an important way for companies to reinvent their company's work cultures, their attitudes towards caregiving leave, paving the way for more engaged workers and in return higher productivity.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Legislation alone will not be able to change the existing culture in our workplaces.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Employers must continue to play a part to encourage working parents to leverage family-friendly workplace policies, such as paid leave and FWAs.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Today, the news of a baby on its way is still very much met with joy, but the "village" now consists of not only of just mothers and fathers, neighbours and extended families, but of employers, bosses, co-workers, human resources and the Government.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I agree that this Bill is a step in the right direction, but for greater sustainability of work-life harmony, let us consider the levers of a modern workplace in flexible work arrangements, which not only supports new parents, but all working parents and caregivers alike.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: As a father of three children, with the youngest being just 14 months old, I am intimately acquainted with the immense joy and profound responsibility that parenthood gives to us.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Within my household, I have proudly taken on the role of the elected or rather, nominated vaccination officer, ensuring my youngest daughter attends all her vaccination appointments.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: There is no privilege greater than cradling our little ones in our arms, offering comfort when they are gripped by fear and pain, especially after the prick of that daunting vaccination needle.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: In such moments, we are starkly reminded of the irreplaceable role that parents play in their children's lives.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Overwhelming scientific evidence reinforces the importance of active father involvement in a child's life.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Esteemed institutions, like the "Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry" have convincingly demonstrated that children, particularly during their infancy, reap immense benefits from the presence and engagement of their fathers.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Their cognitive, emotional and social development receives a substantial boost, laying a strong foundation for their future.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond the personal joys and individual benefits, the father-child bond holds profound implications for our society as a whole.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It moulds the future we are shaping for our children and the society they will inherit.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Policies that support parenthood enhances socio-economic resilience and maturity, which are fundamental to a thriving economy anchored by vibrant businesses and a productive workforce.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Paid paternity leave entitlements vary worldwide, ranging from zero days in the USA to over 50 weeks in Japan and South Korea, though usage often falls short of what is allowed.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore's calibrated increase in paid paternity leave reflects the pragmatic approach to reinforcing our social compact through healthy familial bonds and progressive workplace practices, all while maintaining economic vitality in a tight labour market.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Government and businesses care about the well-being of employees and their families.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Besides paternity leave, businesses also must navigate the challenges of nurturing employees' skills, promoting career advancement and fostering social emotional well-being, all the while maintaining the operational efficiency in a demanding operating environment.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The recently released Singapore Business Federation (SBF) Manpower and Wage Survey indicates that businesses expect that economic conditions will remain weak, with increased business costs as their top challenge.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Despite this, Singapore's labour market remaining robust, with seven consecutive quarters of employment growth and a low unemployment rate of 1.5% as of June.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The introduction of GPPL and UICL enhancements may post significant challenges for certain businesses, especially SMEs.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: With their streamlined workforces, each employee's role is crucial to daily operations.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Frontline service-oriented industries may need to recruit temporary personnel to cover for employees taking extended leaves so that they can maintain minimum staffing levels and service requirements.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: (In English): The Bill aims not to create an uneven playing field or unfairly disadvantage companies constrained by their operating structure.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: To address these limitations and facilitate higher adoption of GPPL and UICL, we can consider the following measures.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The Government could revise the reimbursement schedule for GPPL and GPML.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, these leaves can be taken intermittently within 12 months from the child's birth date, with reimbursement claims permitted only after the last day of leave is utilised.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: With potential increases in paternity leave days, employees may choose to spread their leave over time, causing delays of up to a year in Government reimbursement to companies.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: To alleviate the cash flow strain on SMEs, the Government could consider allowing pro-rated reimbursement filings for GPPL and GPML at more frequent intervals, such as quarterly.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The Government might also consider a tiered support structure to incentivise SMEs and frontline service industries to voluntarily adopt enhanced GPPL arrangements.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This could take the form of higher reimbursement rates for smaller enterprises or enhanced Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) support to assist these companies to adopt staffing and scheduling solutions in managing their workforce deployment effectively.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Such a framework would empower companies, especially SMEs, to enhance their workforce support, aligning it more effectively with their operational and strategic requirements.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This framework could also evaluate a company's contribution and credibility in aligning its practices with national objectives and could be used to acknowledge companies that excel in this area.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This would serve as a powerful incentive for small and medium enterprises.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It is about recognising the profound role fathers play in their children's lives, strengthening families and, ultimately, building a better future for our country.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Let us take this important step together, for the benefit of all.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Parenting today is a shared responsibility between mothers and fathers.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Fathers today are eager to take an active role in parenting and we should support this.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: In many countries, the views on paternity leave are changing as well.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: According to a study by the World Economic Forum, more countries and companies are offering paternity leave benefits to new fathers.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: In OECD countries, men's use of parental leave is increasing overall, even though the number of days taken is still fairly minimal.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Increasing paternity leave is an unequivocal endorsement that fathers play an important role in the family on the arrival of a newborn.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Fathers should be given adequate time to bond with their newborns or adopted children.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: In Estonia, after the end of maternity leave, parents get an additional 435 days off, with compensation calculated at the average of both earnings.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: According to the World Economic Forum, numerous studies have shown that policies promoting father's involvement at home is good for the economy, gender equality and families.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Other studies have also shown that active fatherhood is also good for the men's own health and well-being as well as their relationship with the partners.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Research shows that when men are more involved in the early care of a child, they are more likely to remain connected to that child and to carry out a more equitable amount of care work.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: This Bill is a good step forward, but our work does not end here.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Let us continue to take more progressive steps to be a more equitable and compassionate society where we give our families and children the best possible outcomes.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This Bill is a testament to our nation's commitment to supporting families, recognising the shared responsibilities of parents and ensuring the well-being of our children.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As a father of four, I remember the joyous yet challenging sleepless nights when my children were born.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Those initial weeks were a blur of diaper changes and feeding schedules.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Having an extra two weeks would have made a whole world of difference in sharing the load with my wife and bonding with my newborn.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It promotes flexibility and choice, allowing families to decide what arrangement works best for them.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: By providing additional paternity leave, we are, too, acknowledging the importance of mental well-being of both parents.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Shared responsibilities can alleviate postpartum stress and anxiety, ensuring a healthy mental space for parents.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I recently spoke to a couple who were both working professionals.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The wife, unfortunately, suffered from postpartum depression that lasted a few months and the husband felt really helpless during that period.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: His leave was exhausted and he had to return to work.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This extension of paternity leave would have allowed him to be there for his wife and the newborn in such a critical period.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) might be concerned about the operational challenges posed by extended leave periods.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I spoke to an SME owner who questioned the possible productivity loss during extended leave periods.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: While he supports the idea of paternity leave, he was concerned about the short-term impact on his business.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Perhaps, the Ministry could also carry out a comprehensive review to gauge the long-term effects on SMEs.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I have heard that there should be checks in place to prevent any potential misuse.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: While the term "potential for misuse" often come up in discussions about increased flexibility leave policies, I want to challenge that notion.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In my interactions with constituents and even within my own circle of family and friends, I have found that the overwhelming majority are responsible and would not misuse such a vital support system.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I believe that the key to the success of policies like this is trust – trust in our citizens to use these leaves for the intended purpose of nurturing their families.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: So, in that regard, I urge companies, rather than implementing checks that could deter people from taking leave and perpetuate stigma, we should focus on fostering a culture of responsibility and integrity.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In fact, the more we trust one another, the more we empower them to make ethical choices.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: These, in turn, strengthen our social fabric and make policies like this more effective in the long run.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: While it is natural to have concerns about potential misuse, let us not let these concerns overshadow the larger goal here to support and nurture Singaporean families.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Trust begets trust and it is time we place ours in our people.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The real question is – are we doing enough to foster a society where employers genuinely value and support the family commitments of the employees?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In that regard, could the Ministry share on their efforts to apply, educate and promote the benefits of shared of parental responsibilities and, in the bigger picture, the shared notion of a Singapore Made for Families?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Are there plans to pilot a programme or study to assess the best ways to extend these benefits to such workers?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay):   Sir, I support the amendments to this Act.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This amendment is not just a piece of legislature, but it is also a reflection of our values, aspirations, and commitment to the future of families in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This allows fathers to play a more active role in the early stages of their child's life and also underscores the importance of shared parental responsibilities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It provides flexibility and choice, allowing families to decide what arrangement works best for them.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I am aware that stigma towards utilising family leave is present in our society.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Therefore, we must ensure that we have a public awareness campaign to emphasise the importance of shared responsibility.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It recognises the needs of modern families that is constantly evolving and provides the much-needed support.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: But in line with this progress, let us remember that policies alone are not enough.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We need a paradigm shift in our societal values, where we give priority to holistic development and foster a strong sense of community.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In English): Sir, in conclusion, this Bill is a significant step forward in our commitment to supporting families.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It recognises the evolving needs of modern families and provides the necessary support.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This Bill is not just a piece of legislation.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The amendments will help them to better balance their work responsibilities and the critical task of bringing up the next generation.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One of the most noteworthy provisions of this Bill is the expansion of parental leave options.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Longer parental leave periods not only foster stronger parent-child bonds but also contribute to healthier emotional development in children.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: By extending the duration of paid leave, we empower parents to be present during those crucial early stages of their child's life.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, this Bill addresses the need for fathers to be more involved in the care and nurturing of their children.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Research has shown that the greater involvement of fathers is beneficial for children, contributing positively to their children's physical and cognitive developments.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: More shared parental responsibilities will also support mothers who need to juggle work and household tasks in addition to childcare.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I urge the Ministry to continue to study the effects of these policy reforms on child development, parental well-being and worker productivity.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This information will be used to drive future legislative changes.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For more effective implementation, tighter and more comprehensive collaboration amongst Government agencies, educational institutions and the commercial sector is needed in order to develop a complete support network for families.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These challenges include staffing gaps, business continuity issues and increased operational costs.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: SMEs often operate with smaller workforces compared with larger corporations.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: When employees take extended paternity leave or additional Unpaid Infant Care Leave (UICL), it can result in significant staffing gaps.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Relative to large corporations, SMEs are more vulnerable to the impact of employee absenteeism.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The absence of even one key employee can disrupt the day-to-day operations and put added pressure on the remaining staff.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To manage staffing gaps during extended leaves, SMEs may need to hire part-time or temporary staff.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This can lead to increased operational expenses, which can be especially strenuous in sectors like retail and F&B, where staffing needs are often instantaneous.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The cost of recruiting, training and paying temporary staff can strain the SME's cashflow momentarily.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I am heartened that most of us agree that a collective, whole-of-society effort is needed to build a conducive environment that values and supports families on their parenthood journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Shawn Huang has shared in his speech that the use of paternity leave among the Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries is increasing overall.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have observed a similar trend in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum asked if there is research on the role taken by those fathers who utilise their paternity leave entitlements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our research also showed that fathers found paternity leave useful to support their wives after birth and to settle into the role of fatherhood.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To Ms He Ting Ru's question, we do survey the reasons why fathers do not fully consume their paternity leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A key factor affecting fathers' utilisation of paternity leave is workplace support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes whether supervisors are adequately assuring that using paternity leave will not affect fathers' career prospects and that colleagues are willing to cover the fathers' duties in their absence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to explore ways to encourage employers to support all fathers to use their paternity leave such as by raising awareness of the benefits of providing a family-friendly workplace culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms He Ting Ru also expressed concern on the gap in support for self-employed fathers and those without full-time employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms See Jinli Jean further asked if the Government can consider providing paid paternity leave for the full four-week period of lost income to a self-employed father who stopped working for seven days a week for four weeks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The weekly index of six days takes reference from the Employment Act, which stipulates one rest day per week.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This makes for a common base of reference to employees who receive Government-Paid Paternity Leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked if we could allow parents to use Unpaid Infant Care Leave flexibly during the child's first two years and whether the number of leave days can be increased based on the number of children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Employees may discuss their leave plans with their employers to see how best to meet their needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Mariam Jaafar asked if childcare leave can be increased.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I think many of us as employees would like childcare leave to be increased.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I fully empathise with the challenges Ms Mariam Jaafar had shared that her residents face.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The difficulty is not so much the cost to Government but rather the difficulties faced by employers and businesses who are impacted when leave is made compulsory.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Already, based on the current set of proposals to increase Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) and Unpaid Infant Care Leave (UICL), Members in this House have highlighted concerns from employers that the increased leave provisions will adversely impact their manpower costs and operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Mark Lee in his speech yesterday said, "the introduction of GPPL and UICL enhancements may pose significant challenges for certain businesses, particularly small- and medium-sized enterprises with streamlined workforces where each employee's role is crucial to daily operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Frontline service-oriented industries may need to recruit temporary personnel to cover for employees taking extended leaves." Mr Yip Hon Weng also shared in his speech yesterday, I quote, "appealing for more leave is not a viable solution.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As a small, competitive nation, we must weigh these advancements against its potential effects on businesses, ensuring a balanced approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We must vigilantly track the impact of these policies to discern whether they truly move the needle in the desired direction." These seemingly divergent views show that we need to strike a practical balance between supporting parents in their caregiving responsibilities and meeting employers' manpower needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our leave provisions need to take into account not only the roles of parents as caregivers but also the roles parents play in workplaces as employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I understand that parents with more children will require more leave to take care of their children, should they fall ill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Currently, the Civil Service provides childcare sick leave on a per child basis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This can greatly alleviate parental stress from taking care of more children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To Ms Mariam Jaafar's suggestion, we will look at means, such as surveys, to gauge the take-up rate of UICL.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Mariam Jaafar asked for the equalisation of parental leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked the Ministry to consider providing adoptive and foster parents with more GPPL and UICL.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Maternity leave is provided for mothers to recuperate physically from childbirth and care for and bond with their newborn.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Hence, it is longer than paternity leave, which allows for fathers to care for their wives and bond with their newborn child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is also why maternity leave is longer than adoption leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To Ms Hany Soh's query, we currently do not intend to change the Shared Parental Leave provision under this Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is why beyond the minimal stipulations for maternity leave and paternity leave, any additional leave that the Government may consider in future will likely be of a shared nature, as per our move on shared parental leave in 2013.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On fostering, unlike adoption, fostering is a temporary care arrangement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To better support adoptive and foster parents, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and our community partners offer a range of services to meet their needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: All new foster parents are also trained by the Social Service Institute to care for foster children and can receive advice from more experienced foster parents through peer support networks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To defray the costs of caring for a foster child, MSF provides a monthly fostering allowance as well as childcare and medical subsidies for the foster children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Desmond Choo expressed concern that some self-employed fathers may not qualify for GPPL if they take time off from work to support their wives in the pre-delivery phase.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They will not be disqualified simply because they took some time off work during this period.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms See Jinli Jean has asked the Government to consider disbursing a self-employed person’s claim for lost income at the start of his or her leave period rather than after it has concluded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I wish to clarify that claims for leave or income lost are processed on a reimbursement basis to ensure that the leave has been taken as intended first before payment is made.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This also helps with the computation of the actual amount of income lost to be reimbursed, which would not be possible to ascertain until the leave has been taken.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Hany Soh asked if flexibility could be exercised to allow expectant mothers to consume their maternity leave earlier in their final trimester.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Expectant mothers who need to absent themselves from work earlier than 28 days before can tap on their sick leave or hospitalisation leave if they feel unwell, for example, if they suffer from severe nausea in the first trimester.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members such as Mr Yip Hon Weng, Dr Wan Rizal, Mr Don Wee and Assoc Prof Razwana Begum have asked about the Government’s efforts in encouraging fathers to utilise paternity leave as well as to normalise paternity leave and the importance of shared parental responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Ms Yeo Wan Ling has stated, societal norms must be considered in the discussion of encouraging take-up of parental leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is important that the society adopts a mindset that embraces paternal involvement from the onset.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To promote active fatherhood and the importance of shared parental responsibilities, we have been working with community partners such as the Families for Life Council and the Centre for Fathering on three key family movements in Singapore – the Families for Life, Dads for Life and Mums for Life movements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These movements look at strengthening family ties and resilience with the aim of increasing marriage stability as well as advocating the importance of shared parenting and household responsibilities between mothers and fathers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, the Centre for Fathering runs several campaigns throughout the year to reinforce and signal the importance of fathers’ active involvement in their child’s development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: One of the campaigns is the Great Companies for Dads Awards, which engages and recognises companies that nurture a family-friendly work culture through their policies and initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The attitudes and mindsets of supervisors and colleagues also make a big difference in helping fathers feel assured that they are not being discriminated for using their leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We also hope to encourage self-employed persons to recognise the benefits of parental leave and how the Government tries to support them through the provision of Government-paid paternity benefits and Government-Paid Paternity and Maternity Leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To Ms Hany Soh’s questions, we had indeed sought employers’ views and feedback on the leave enhancements through our consultations with the tripartite partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue working with our tripartite partners to encourage employers to foster family-friendly workplace cultures that will better support parents in managing their work and family responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We also encourage employers to be supportive and understanding when fathers take paternity leave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This would help employees be more motivated, like what Ms Yeo Wan Ling has shared.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the long run, progressive employers can stand to benefit from better talent attraction and retention.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To Mr Melvin Yong's suggestion to conduct a local study to examine companies that offer the best work-life balance, we will look at best practices today to identify what other companies can adopt.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum asked whether gig workers would benefit from the increase in Government-Paid Paternity Leave, and if not, what support is available to compensate them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Don Wee suggested launching a public awareness campaign so that more parents are aware of their leave entitlements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Desmond Choo also asked if the Government could broaden its work with the trade associations and chambers (TACs) and the Labour Movement to spread awareness of the enhanced Government-Paid Paternity Leave, especially among the self-employed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government will work closely with our tripartite partners to raise awareness of these benefits among employees and the self-employed, including gig workers, to encourage them to utilise their leave or benefits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, we have developed an infographic and produced a video on parental leave targeted at raising awareness among self-employed persons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The infographic was disseminated through our tripartite partners’ networks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to build on these efforts and look for ways to further raise awareness and encourage parents to utilise their leave benefits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Don Wee asked if we will consider conducting a review to assess the impact of leave enhancements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Mr Shawn Huang and Ms Usha Chandradas have said, it is a continuous process to review our policies to meet the evolving needs of parents and to make our society more family friendly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will monitor the impact of our leave enhancements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Mark Lee suggested revising the reimbursement schedule of the Government-Paid Maternity Leave and Paternity Leave to more frequent intervals to alleviate cash flow strain on SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We recognise that some employers may have concerns with parents taking additional parental leave due to the nature of the work and challenge of finding covering arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the meantime, employers and employees may exercise flexibility in the parents’ utilisation of parental leave, such as by taking the leave in more than one period within their child’s first year, to minimise disruptions to business operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parents should also play their part by discussing their leave arrangements with their employers in advance, so that their employers can plan for the necessary covering arrangements and any additional resources that they may require.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I also thank Mr Desmond Choo for sharing that the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) is ready to help our SMEs to develop policies that will better support parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Another important strategy for companies to build agility in manpower needs is through the adoption of flexible workplace arrangements (FWAs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As mentioned by Ms Yeo Wan Ling, FWAs are more sustainable options and can benefit not just parents of young children but also other caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When implemented well, FWAs can increase productivity, lower absenteeism and turnover, which in turn can help companies mitigate the effects of manpower constraints.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Melvin Yong suggested expanding the Child Development Co-Savings Act (CDCA) to provide incentives to employers who provide good FWAs to employees with children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We review the scope of the CDCA periodically to best serve the needs of parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For FWAs however, they benefit not just parents but also caregivers of other familial members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As such, incentivising FWAs may take other forms other than through amending the CDCA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We share Members’ views on the importance of having FWAs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And the Government is on the lookout for positive examples of such companies to share with others at opportune times.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We take heart that some companies have already walked this path and found success.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Take, for example, 1AND8 Singapore Pte Ltd, the company behind the Museum of Ice Cream.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They have adopted the Tripartite Standard on Flexible Work Arrangements and allow their staff to fully telecommute, only returning to the office for physical meetings when required.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The company also practises staggered hours and has part-time work available for their frontline Guest Specialist Experience positions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This approach has helped the company to boost work productivity while also enabling their employees to achieve a better work-life balance, leading to increased job satisfaction and higher morale.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The positive outcomes are evident in their employees staying with them for extended periods, contributing to a lower turnover rate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Mark Lee suggested establishing a comprehensive framework to recognise companies that support national-level initiatives such as the Tripartite Standard and progressive wages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, companies that adopt the Tripartite Standards will be profiled with the TS logo on MyCareersFuture job portal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This allows them to gain greater visibility in talent recruitment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This can encourage consumers and service buyers to prioritise purchases from them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will now address comments raised by Members about extending support to caregivers of other dependants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if the different leave schemes could be amalgamated into a family care leave scheme to provide flexibility for parents and caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, the leave schemes are differentiated to cater to the needs of different caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They are also calibrated to balance between employees’ caregiving needs and employers’ business costs and manpower needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Usha Chandradas, Ms See Jinli Jean and Mr Desmond Choo have also called for more support for familial caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today’s Bill is on the CDCA and so we are discussing maternity and paternity leave and benefits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On the broader topic of support for caregivers for the elderly, I would like to assure Members that your feedback will be provided to the agencies looking into this topic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond legislated leave provisions, it is important that we bring all stakeholders including employers to build a family-friendly work environment, so that caregivers can better manage both their work and caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On the Child Development Account (CDA), Ms Hany Soh has asked for greater flexibility on how funds can be utilised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The range of approved CDA usages is circumscribed to ensure that the funds are well-utilised to the benefit of the child.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Nonetheless, we do regularly review the CDA scheme, together with our suite of marriage and parenthood policies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Over the years, we have enhanced the CDA scheme to provide more support to parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, we have increased the Government co-matching contributions and also introduced the CDA First Step Grant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also expanded the areas where the CDA funds can be used and will continue to review how this can be further refined.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Ong Hua Han asked if the CDA co-matching or the CDA First Step Grant could be increased to better support children with disabilities to cope with the cost of living.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These schemes are designed on a broad basis to support all parents in raising their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government is also working to expand places in early intervention services, SPED schools and SSCCs to ensure that children with special needs can access an education that develops their potential and equips them with knowledge and skills to participate meaningfully in society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Ong Hua Han also asked if the income threshold of means-tested schemes such as the Assistive Technology Fund and Enabling Transport Subsidy can be revised to align with the median household per capita income.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He suggested factoring in actual costs borne by families as part of the means-testing calculations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: MSF regularly reviews the income thresholds for such schemes to ensure that households receive the help that they need and we will take in his inputs when reviewing all these schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
